item.title: Hunger in Healdsburg – A Community Conversation — Thu Oct 1, 10:30 AM — Abel De Luna Community Center
item.description:
**Hunger is happening in Healdsburg—and Healdsburg organizations are stepping up to help.**
Food insecurity affects thousands of individuals and families in Healdsburg—neighbors who are working, raising families, and contributing to our community, yet still struggling to put enough food on the table.
**Hunger in Healdsburg: A Community Conversation** brings together local hunger relief organizations, community leaders, and residents for an open and informative dialogue about food insecurity in Healdsburg. This event is free for all to attend and is designed to create space for listening, learning, and connection—centering the voices of organizations that are directly serving our community.
Hosted by the Redwood Empire Food Bank, in partnership with the City of Healdsburg, this event will highlight:
\- What food insecurity looks like in Healdsburg today
\- The local programs and partnerships working to address hunger
\- How collaboration and community engagement make a meaningful

item.title: Chris Jorgensen Gallery Evening and Norwegian Folk Art — Thu Oct 1, 5:00 PM — Sonoma State Historic Park
item.description:
The Christian Jorgensen Gallery inside the Mission at Sonoma State Historic Park\) will be open 5 P.M.-7 P.M., Thursday, October 1st! This will be our final Sonoma Art Walk event of the 2026 season. We will be celebrating Jorgensen's October Birthday and the Gallery's 75th Anniversary! The gallery features 57 original watercolor paintings of California missions that Chris Jorgensen created between 1903 and 1905. We’ll do a deep dive into the exquisite details of C.J.’s paintings with tools and materials provided. In honor of C.J.'s Norwegian heritage, Sonoma State Historic Park is pleased to collaborate with Sons of Norway, Freya Lodge of Santa Rosa. The lodge will present a collection of traditional Norwegian folk arts which will be on display at the central table inside the gallery. Enjoy live music of Norway while perusing the art, plus other surprises! Free admission.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: The Arts Guild of Sonoma Presents: A Harvest of Art — Thu Oct 1, 5:00 PM — Arts Guild of Sonoma
item.description:
The Arts Guild of Sonoma presents: A Harvest of Art, September 30–November 2, featuring Monica Kuhlman Jacobson’s Sea and Sand coastal photography, Deirdre Molloy’s distinctive mixed-media portraits, and new original works by Guild member artists. Reception Thursday November 2, 5-7PM. Meet the artists. Voted Best Gallery 2026 People's Choice Awards. Now in its 49th year, the Arts Guild of Sonoma is one of California’s longest-running artist cooperatives. The Guild showcases the creative voices of Bay Area artists through exhibitions, community engagement, and educational programs. A 501\(c\)\(3\) nonprofit organization, the Guild is committed to supporting regional artists and fostering opportunities for young and emerging creators, including Sonoma Valley high school students. Gallery open to the public Wednesdays through Mondays 11am to 5pm.140 E Napa Street, Sonoma. www.artsguildofsonoma.org

item.title: AI Series: Conversation with Z Zeng — Fri Oct 2, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Z works at the intersection of operations, design, and AI, helping organizations scale through better systems, stronger alignment, and more effective teams. She currently leads Experience Operations at Deel, a global leader in people technology, focusing on end-to-end AI enablement across products, teams, and operations. Most recently, she led a five-month AI transformation initiative at Cloudflare, advancing AI literacy and practical adoption across teams. An entrepreneur and educator, Z is passionate about operational excellence and creating environments where teams can do their best work. Throughout her career, she has led design organizations in-house and in consulting, taught leadership and interaction design, and mentored the next generation of designers. Outside of work, Z co-creates a sci-fi series and paints large-scale floral artworks, reflecting her passion for creativity both at work and beyond.

item.title: Fall in the Garden: Planting and Caring for your California Natives — Sun Oct 4, 10:30 AM — Petaluma Bounty
item.description:
Join Sonoma County Master Gardeners Dandi Hagler and Kim Jacobs for a workshop on how to care for your California native plants this fall.
They'll walk through which plants benefit from pruning now versus later in the season, and how to identify plants that are setting seed, which provide valuable food sources for birds and other wildlife. They'll also cover broader plant care guidelines to keep your garden healthy year-round, along with irrigation strategies for newly installed plants. Whether you're adding California natives for the first time or maintaining what you already have, you'll leave with actionable advice on what to do now.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

In this class you will learn how to create a lush and fragrant holiday wreath using a wire frame and foliage, branches, and other dried materials. Whether you're a novice or a seasoned crafter, this workshop offers a warm and welcoming environment for all skill levels.
Silvia Bagnacani is a professional artist, educator, and floral designer with a passion for celebrating the beauty of seasonal blooms. Known around Sonoma for her inspiring floral arranging and wreath-making workshops, Silvia thoughtfully sources local flowers and foliage to create stunning, nature-inspired designs.
